---
title: 'Introduction'
description: "Recolor Discord's interface with a theme."
icon: 'paintbrush'
---

A theme changes how Discord looks. It is **data**: a JSON definition of colors (and an optional background) that Unbound applies to Discord's interface. A [plugin](/plugins/introduction), by contrast, is code that runs.

### How themes work

Discord styles its UI from a palette of named colors. A theme overrides that palette: you set values for the color names you want to change, and Unbound applies them to the app. A theme is parsed JSON with no `start`/`stop` to run. Selecting or removing one updates the saved choice right away, but the colors change on the next restart (see below).

Themes use the same [manager](/modules/managers) as plugins, and go through the same lifecycle: loaded, enabled, disabled, and persisted. The difference is that enabling a theme *applies* it. Only one theme is active at a time, so enabling a new one replaces the previous one.

<Note>
	Colors are applied **natively**, not from JavaScript. At startup, the loader reads your theme's `bundle.json` and swizzles Discord's color lookups. A theme takes effect only after a restart, and no JavaScript hook can recolor a running app. See [Theme Types](/themes/types) for the bundle's shape.
</Note>

### What a theme defines

<CardGroup cols={2}>
	<Card title='Manifest' icon='circle-info' href='/addons/manifest'>
		Metadata that identifies your theme: name, authors, version.
	</Card>
	<Card title='Theme Types' icon='palette' href='/themes/types'>
		The semantic and raw colors that make up the palette, and the base type they extend.
	</Card>
	<Card title='Backgrounds' icon='image' href='/themes/backgrounds'>
		An optional image behind the interface, with blur and opacity.
	</Card>
</CardGroup>

<Note>
	A theme can't run logic or patch components. It only restyles. For behavior, write a [plugin](/plugins/introduction).
</Note>
